faq.title: Good to know before you start

app.q: Do my customers need to install an app?
app.a: No. They get a link by email, or scan the QR code you hand them, and follow their item in their browser. No account, no app.

software.q: Do I have to give up my till or shop software?
software.a: No. ReadyYet doesn't replace your till or your management software, it adds tracking for your customers. You log the item at the counter in a few seconds and carry on working as before.

notified.q: How does my customer hear about it?
notified.a: By email: when the item is logged, when a quote or some information is waiting on them, when the expected date moves back and when it's ready, with a reminder if they don't come by. They can also open their tracking page whenever they like.

sms.a: No. Tracking works by email and QR code, which costs nothing extra, for you or your customers. If a customer prefers, you send them their link on WhatsApp in one click.

start.q: How long does it take to get started?
start.a: A few minutes. You create your shop, your trade's steps are already set up, and you log your first Ticket straight away.

afterTrial.q: What happens after the free trial?
afterTrial.a: You pick Essentiel or Pro for each shop. Without a subscription your data stays, but you can't create new Tickets.

shops.a: Yes. Each shop has its own subscription, team and steps, and you switch between them from the same account.

guide.title: Repair tracking built for shoe repair shops
paragraphs: Behind a cobbler's counter, the shelves fill up fast: resoles, heels, sole guards, bags to stitch, zips to replace. Every customer wants to know when to come back, and most of them ask by phone. With ReadyYet, each drop-off becomes a Ticket with its own tracking page the customer opens on their phone.

At the counter, you note the customer's name, the item and the expected date. They get their link by email, on WhatsApp or by scanning a QR code. Their page shows where things stand, from Received to Repairing to Ready, along with your address and opening hours.

When the pair is ready, an email goes out on its own. If nobody comes, a reminder follows after 3 days and again after 10, so forgotten shoes finally leave the shelf. On Pro, you add your own steps, like a diagnosis for leather goods or a quote to approve before a big job.

after: Customers see how their pair is doing on their phone.
An email goes out when it's ready, then reminders after 3 and 10 days.
They come in once, when the work is done.

guide.title: Order tracking built for dry cleaners
paragraphs: A dry cleaner runs on drop-offs: the week's shirts, a suit for a wedding, a delicate dress, a duvet before summer. Customers come back too early, or forget their clothes for weeks. ReadyYet gives every drop-off a tracking page that says how the order is doing and when it's waiting.

The Ticket takes seconds at the counter, with the items and the expected date. The customer gets their link by email or by scanning a QR code, then sees Received, Cleaning and Ready, plus your opening hours, without ringing you.

As soon as the order is ready, the customer gets an email. If they don't come, a reminder goes out after 3 and 10 days, and your rail empties faster. When a stain takes longer, you push the date back and the customer is emailed the new one.

guide.title: Order tracking built for picture framers
paragraphs: A poster, a canvas, a diploma, a piece of embroidery: every frame is made to order, often with a few weeks' lead time. Your customers wonder how their piece is coming along. ReadyYet gives them a tracking page that answers any time.

When the order is placed, you create a Ticket with the piece, the moulding and the expected date. The customer gets their link by email or QR code and follows Received, In progress, Quality check and Ready.

Once the frame is done, attach a photo: the customer sees it on their page before coming in. They're emailed as soon as it's ready, then reminded after 3 and 10 days if they're slow, so finished frames stop taking up room meant for new ones.
